column4: You could try the patience of a saint. If you bring up your son's exam results one more time I'm going to lose it!

column4: Well, speaking of stubborn people, Justin could try the patience of a saint. The other day he even made Brian raise his voice!

column3: Seguro que probaría a hacer tiro con arco si tuviera la más mínima oportunidad.

column4: If she can't kick the habit, it won't be for want of trying.

column4: She was absolutely devastated when she couldn't kick the habit. It really wasn't for want of trying.

column4: Her mother was thrilled to bits when she let slip that they were trying for a baby.

column4: I was truly gladdened by the news that they are trying for a baby.

column4: Beaming from ear to ear, she said to her husband: "Let's try for a baby!"

column4: Do you like this card I made for Julia? No, I don't! Well, you couldn't do it if you tried!

column4: Ladies couldn't ignore me if they tried! Look at me! I'm gorgeous, aren't I? If you say so...

column4: Andrew Karel is my favourite player. But he couldn't score a goal if he tried!

column4: How do you survive without chorizo? Look! Being a vegetarian isn't that bad, don't knock it till you've tried it!

column3: ¡No puedo creer que bailes salsa! Bailar salsa es divertido, no lo descartes hasta probarlo.
column4: I can't believe you dance salsa! Dancing salsa is a lot of fun! Don't knock it till you've tried it!

column4: That's foul! How can you eat that? Pasta and ketchup is actually quite tasty, don't knock it until you've tried it!

column4: I buy girls flowers, chocolates and I write them poems, but I'm still single! Mate, I think you're trying too hard.

column4: Does this cap match my boots? Don't you think you're trying a little too hard to be stylish?

column4: When water freezes it expands by 10%. You're trying too hard to sound intelligent again. Stop!

column4: Whatever you do, kids, don't try this at home; it's far too dangerous.

column4: I'm going to jump this river on my motorbike. One wrong move could be fatal. Don't try this at home!

column4: I'm about to have a go at breaking the record for the longest time on a crocodile's back. Don't try this at home!

column4: Our next challenge is to drive this car blindfolded and follow the instructions. Don't try this at home!

column3: Intentaré hacerle entrar en razón.
column4: I'll attempt to make him see reason.

column4: You made a really brave attempt.

column4: She passed her driving test on the first attempt.

column4: The king's army strived in vain to quell the uprising.

column4: You could at least make an effort!

column4: He's made absolutely no effort to get to know my family.

column4: I was touched. They all made such an effort.

column4: You really must sample this divine Bordeaux.

column4: I would very much like to sample the champagne. I've heard it's an exquisite vintage.

column4: She went through the trials and tribulations of getting an Australian travel visa, only to realize that she couldn't afford to go.

column4: Many books have been written about the trials and tribulations of being a teenager.

column4: Sometimes, the best way to learn how to cook is by trial and error. Nobody is born a world-class chef!

column4: There are certain trades in the labour market that cannot be learned by trial and error, for safety reasons.

column4: Learning by trial and error helps you to become a good problem solver. It also helps you to cope with failure.

column4: It's a good thing we gave him a 6-month trial period, because now I see that he's just not cut out for this job!

column4: Let's go out for cocktails to celebrate the fact that I've just successfully finished my 6-month trial period!

column4: I'm going to volunteer to participate in some clinical trials so that I can afford to fund my trip to Europe.
